recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-42807 unless the work group later decides to revise the inherited FHIR-41225 canonical/XOR modeling.
issue_request: FHIR-42807 was an Applied FHIR-I change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked for ExampleScenario actors to be able to point to ActorDefinition by adding a 0..1 definition element, with wording that the title and description in ExampleScenario may differ from the formal definition and that the type SHALL be the same.
initial_application: The main actor definition element was introduced by related Applied issue FHIR-41225 in commit b7141f572474eaca235597fe385c4f5dc3e31a64, which added ExampleScenario.actor.definition, relaxed ExampleScenario.actor.type to 0..1, and added the exs-24 one-of type/definition invariant. FHIR-42807 itself was then applied by commit 2f9a07f8b7d1967dc0bdeb4490dec206b9419937, adding the requested comment to ExampleScenario.actor.definition. PR #3299 merged those ActorDefinition/ExampleScenario changes.
additional_context: FHIR-41225 clarified that the reference should be a canonical URL and its approved resolution says to add ExampleScenario.actor.definition as canonical(ActorDefinition), so the current canonical type is the later precise representation of the requested ActorDefinition link rather than a missing Reference datatype. source/fhir.ini actively lists both examplescenario and actordefinition resources under the FHIR-I work group. Confluence FHIR-I minutes confirm the FHIR-42807 vote, and a targeted Zulip search found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already has ExampleScenario.actor.definition 0..1 with targetProfile ActorDefinition, the requested comment, and the related one-of type/definition invariant from FHIR-41225.
